steps.label: KP02 Linear classifiers | Guided study
01 · Shared covariance cancels quadratic terms · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Female: Used on this page: both classes share ;  x is the feature vector and  w_i,c_i are linear coefficients.

What boundary remains after common terms cancel?

steps.label: 01 · Shared covariance cancels quadratic terms · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: g_i= w_i^T x+c_i with  w_i=^-1μ_i; their difference contains no quadratic term.

steps.label: 01 · Shared covariance cancels quadratic terms · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: A linear boundary follows from shared spread, not from collinear samples.

steps.label: 02 · A larger prior gives a class more space · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Male: Used on this page: means (0,0),(4,0) and =I; the prior ratio changes from 1:1 to 4:1.

Which class should get more space?

steps.label: 02 · A larger prior gives a class more space · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: The shift is σ^2(P_1/P_2)/\|μ_1-μ_2\|=0.3466, toward the less probable class two.

steps.label: 02 · A larger prior gives a class more space · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Prior shifts move the boundary to enlarge the more common class region.

steps.label: 03 · More spread makes the same prior change move the boundary farther · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Female: Used on this page: log prior ratio 4, mean separation 4, and common variance σ^2.

Does more spread produce a larger shift?

steps.label: 03 · More spread makes the same prior change move the boundary farther · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Δ=σ^24/4 gives shifts 0.1733 and 0.8664.

steps.label: 03 · More spread makes the same prior change move the boundary farther · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: Shared covariance still affects a linear boundary; it does not disappear from the model.

steps.label: 04 · Practice: change the prior ratio to e · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Male: Used on this page: means (0,0),(4,0), σ^2=1, and prior ratio e with  e=1.

Find the shift, then the new boundary.

steps.label: 04 · Practice: change the prior ratio to e · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: With class one at zero and class two at four, a larger class-one prior expands its region to the right.

steps.label: 04 · Practice: change the prior ratio to e · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Verify the direction as well as the magnitude of the shift.

steps.label: 05 · Correlation turns the normal without curving the boundary · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Female: Used on this page: means (0,0),(4,0), equal priors, and =[smallmatrix2&1.2\\1.2&1.5smallmatrix].

How is the mean difference transformed?

steps.label: 05 · Correlation turns the normal without curving the boundary · 2/3
05 · Correlation turns the normal without curving the boundary · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: With general covariance, the boundary is perpendicular to the transformed mean difference.

steps.label: 06 · Practice: remove correlation and find the normal · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Male: Used on this page: means (0,0),(4,0), equal priors, and =diag(2,1.5).

Where does the normal point without correlation?

steps.label: 06 · Practice: remove correlation and find the normal · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: The inverse is diag(1/2,2/3). Multiplying a horizontal mean difference leaves a zero vertical component.

steps.label: 06 · Practice: remove correlation and find the normal · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Unequal axis scales can remain even when this boundary returns to vertical.

steps.label: 07 · Mahalanobis distance discounts directions differently · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Female: Used on this page: d_m^2=(x-μ)^T^-1(x-μ), with center μ and spread .

Is moving along the long axis equally far?

steps.label: 07 · Mahalanobis distance discounts directions differently · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: With =^T, rotated coordinates give d_m^2=Σ_j y_j^2/_j; eigenvectors are columns of .

steps.label: 07 · Mahalanobis distance discounts directions differently · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: Displacements along a broad direction cost less in Mahalanobis distance.

steps.label: 08 · The same point can change class when the metric changes · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Male: Used on this page: x=(1,2.2), means (0,0),(3,3), and =[smallmatrix1.1&0.3\\0.3&1.9smallmatrix].

Can the nearest center change with the metric?

steps.label: 08 · The same point can change class when the metric changes · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: ^-1=[smallmatrix0.95&-0.15\\-0.15&0.55smallmatrix] gives squared Mahalanobis distances 2.952 and 3.672.

steps.label: 08 · The same point can change class when the metric changes · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: The nearest class depends on how the metric represents spread.

steps.label: 09 · Practice: move the query near the first center · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Female: Used on this page: x=(0.5,0.5), means (0,0),(3,3), and inverse covariance [smallmatrix0.95&-0.15\\-0.15&0.55smallmatrix].

What changes near the first center?

steps.label: 09 · Practice: move the query near the first center · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Both metrics now favor class one. The original reversal was a specific example, not a requirement at every point.

steps.label: 09 · Practice: move the query near the first center · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: Changing the metric can change decisions without changing every point.

steps.label: 10 · Practice: move the second center down and right · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Male: Used on this page: x=(1,2.2), means (0,0),(3,-3), and covariance [smallmatrix1.1&0.3\\0.3&1.9smallmatrix].

Compare values before choosing a class.

steps.label: 10 · Practice: move the second center down and right · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: The new difference is (-2,5.2); both metrics make it larger than the distance to class one.

steps.label: 10 · Practice: move the second center down and right · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Fix both the data and metric before comparing classes.

steps.label: 11 · A common translation preserves relative distances · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Female: Used on this page: add the same vector c to every sample and mean, keeping the same .

Can a common translation change who is closer?

steps.label: 11 · A common translation preserves relative distances · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: The common c cancels. Both Euclidean and fixed-covariance Mahalanobis distances remain unchanged.

steps.label: 11 · A common translation preserves relative distances · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: Relative geometry, rather than a shared choice of origin, determines the decision.

steps.label: 12 · Maximum score and minimum distance are equivalent here · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Male: Used on this page: equal priors and shared , with d_i^2=(x-μ_i)^T^-1(x-μ_i).

Why does a minus sign turn a minimum into a maximum?

steps.label: 12 · Maximum score and minimum distance are equivalent here · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Female: g_i=-12d_i^2+const. Unequal priors add  P_i, so plain nearest-mean selection is insufficient.

steps.label: 12 · Maximum score and minimum distance are equivalent here · 3/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Explicit assumptions let scores and distances verify one another.

steps.label: 13 · Different class covariances can retain curvature · 1/3
steps.speakerNotes:
Female: Used on this page: class covariances _1,_2; quadratic terms cancel when the two match.

When can quadratic terms no longer cancel?

steps.label: 13 · Different class covariances can retain curvature · 2/3
steps.speakerNotes: Male: Different covariances generally give quadratic differences; degenerate special cases can still be linear.
